clue.text: Gather a group discussed …

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a group of workers or sailors is a crew, so these words give a crew

explanation.surface: Someone collects a team of people for a talk, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, which continues the sentence; each clue still works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gather is to build up or amass over time, as interest does in a bank account.

clue.text: The dregs, say, breaking into strongbox to get money (not pence)

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece forces its way inside the box

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox for valuables
eg, for example, is what say signals

indicators.note: not means the letter for pence is removed

parts.note: pounds are money in Britain

explanation.surface: A thief breaks into a safe for cash but finds no small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' here is the familiar signal for an example (EG), while 'not pence' strips the P from the money. 'breaking into' has the example force its way inside the strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sediment left at the bottom of a cafetière after brewing is a kind of dregs.

clue.text: Once more apportion substantial amount

parts.note: real means substantial, having actual substance
a lot is an amount or batch

explanation.surface: Someone shares out a large quantity again.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefix sense: to distribute or allocate again, the prefix meaning a second time.

clue.text: One showing brief urge to consume single portion

indicators.note: to consume means the shortened word swallows the other pieces
brief means the word for urge is cut short at its end

parts.note: to exhort is to urge strongly
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a bit is a portion

explanation.surface: Someone shows a short-lived craving for one helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the word for urge; 'to consume' has what remains swallow the single portion. 'showing' suggests revealing a feeling, but defines a person who displays work.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone displaying work at a gallery, fair or show is one presenting it to the public.

clue.text: … his endless rock arrangement for singers

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the word rock loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its end is removed

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone arranges his rock music for a group of vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims rock to ROC; 'arrangement' rearranges HIS with ROC. 'arrangement' looks like a musical term but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: church or school vocal ensembles are groups of singers, so the plural fits the plural definition.

clue.text: Well I never, finally I'm in charge of inquest

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like well
I as a digit is one

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of never

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise followed by someone announcing they run an inquiry into a death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well I never' reads as one stock exclamation, but each word works separately; 'finally' takes only the end of never. The definition is spoken in the first person, borrowing the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Role: the official who leads inquiries into sudden or unexplained deaths would say this of their job.

clue.text: Former athlete has to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve means to keep something within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to own is to have, so has gives owns
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A retired sportsperson must save their stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: Jesse Owens was the American sprinter who won four golds at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jesse Owens, the American track star of the 1930s, is a sportsman of the past.

clue.text: Alarm beginning to go off? Correct

indicators.note: beginning to go off means the opening letter of the word for alarm is removed

parts.note: to alarm is to frighten

explanation.surface: Asks whether an alarm clock is about to ring, then says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' looks like an alarm sounding, but it signals the loss of the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to put right or set straight, as a verb.

clue.text: Wee heart pounds during boxing match? Mine might

definitions.text: Wee heart pounds during boxing match? Mine might

indicators.note: during means the rearranged letters sit within the word for a bout

parts.note: a boxing match is a fight

indicators.note: pounds means beats hard, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A small boxer admits their little heart races in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like a heartbeat (or a weight) but shuffles the first two words; 'during' sets them within the bout. The whole clue is spoken by a light boxer, so it also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boxer in one of the lightest weight divisions might well say a small heart pounds in a bout.

clue.text: Article introducing art exhibition in Welsh woman's book

parts.note: the is the definite article, coming first here

indicators.note: in means the exhibition goes inside the name

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh woman's name, with the possessive adding s
a salon is an exhibition of art, as in the Paris Salon

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece previews a gallery show featured in a Welsh woman's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Sian is a common Welsh girl's name; 'in' places the exhibition within it. 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece but is just the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Thessalonians is a pair of epistles of Paul in the New Testament of the Bible.

clue.text: Aquatic creature and where it can be found, live

parts.note: the creature lives in the sea
L marks the live wire on an electrical plug, alongside N for neutral and E for earth

explanation.surface: A description of a sea animal and its habitat, followed by an odd extra word.
explanation.walkthrough: On British plugs the live terminal is marked L, which is the convention used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a whiskered marine mammal that swims in the sea and rests on rocks or ice.

clue.text: Old hospital worker giving sustenance to dog?

parts.note: a bone is food given to a dog
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: Asks who in a hospital of the past was charged with feeding a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving ... to' joins the pieces: a bone given to a setter. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical role: someone who reset fractured or dislocated limbs, before orthopaedic surgery became a specialism.

clue.text: It's eaten by a wild beast in Florida, one causing trouble

indicators.note: eaten by means the first word is swallowed inside the beast

parts.note: gator is the American short form of alligator, common in Florida swamps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something gets devoured by an alligator in Florida, which is called a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' puts It inside the beast; gator is everyday American shorthand for an alligator.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who stirs up unrest or protest, a troublemaker or rabble-rouser.

clue.text: Outlaw is reverse of popular, gatecrashing party

indicators.note: gatecrashing means barging into the party uninvited, so one piece goes inside it

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: reverse of says the word for popular is read backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An outlaw is the opposite of a popular figure, turning up uninvited to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link; 'reverse of' turns the word for popular backwards and 'gatecrashing' pushes it into the party. 'Outlaw' is a verb here, not a bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to outlaw something is to prohibit or expel it, as a verb.

clue.text: Unsettled during fight, withdrawing

indicators.note: during means the word for unsettled sits within the fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight or boxing contest
a debt still owing is unsettled

explanation.surface: A boxer, rattled mid-contest, retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' suggests nerves but means unpaid, like a debt still due.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: retiring or withdrawing from a role or contest, often gracefully.

clue.text: Post Office worker unsettled by roster

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A postal employee is upset by the work rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges the letters of ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone in a mail office who divides letters and parcels by destination.

clue.text: Native group accommodates a French legionary officer

indicators.note: accommodates means the group gives room to the other piece inside

parts.note: a tribe is a native group of people
un is French for a

explanation.surface: An indigenous people take in a French Foreign Legion officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' gives the French article room inside the group. 'legionary' points to ancient Rome, not the French Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical role: a senior officer in a Roman legion was a military tribune.

clue.text: Poorly in the end, after concoction of cold raw chicken

indicators.note: after means this letter comes behind the mixed letters
a concoction mixes ingredients, so these letters are mixed up
in the end picks the final letter of poorly

explanation.surface: A dish of uncooked cold chicken leaves someone feeling ill eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction of' rearranges COLD RAW into COWARDL, and 'in the end' takes Y from Poorly, placed 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: calling someone chicken means they are timid and lacking courage.

clue.text: Weather generally cold near S American capital, note

indicators.note: near means these pieces sit beside each other

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A weather report notes chilly conditions around a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning: the prevailing conditions of an area over a long period, rather than day to day.

clue.text: Rate cut by bank makes you more bad-tempered

indicators.note: cut means the word rate loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it loses its end
a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bank's interest rate reduction makes customers grumpier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by bank' reads as a central bank decision; really 'cut' trims RATE to RAT, followed by TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal comparative: ratty means irritable, so this is more irritable.

clue.text: Hint I'll come ahead of small boy in race

indicators.note: come ahead of means the letter stands at the front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the boy's name goes inside the word for race

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
Tim is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will arrive before a young lad competing in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come ahead of' puts I at the front, and 'in' places the small boy's name inside the race, meaning a people rather than a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an indirect suggestion or clue to something, as a noun.

clue.text: Hate a house with brown exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the brown abbreviation goes on the outside of the house abbreviation

parts.note: BR is a standard abbreviation for brown

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a home with brown outside walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Both house and brown are standard two-letter abbreviations; 'exterior' puts brown on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detest or loathe something intensely, as a verb.

clue.text: Very small quantity of peat in Yorkshire

indicators.note: quantity of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little amount of moorland peat found in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quantity of' looks like part of the surface but points to letters spanning PEAT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: minute, minuscule, extremely little in size.

clue.text: Scholar worried about Open University test ultimately in a state

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
worried means agitated, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK distance-learning university

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of test

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic gets anxious over a distance-learning exam and ends up in a fretful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges SCHOLAR into SHCAROL, which goes 'about' OU plus T (from test 'ultimately'). 'in a state' looks like a phrase meaning upset; only 'state' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the fifty members of the USA, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Fellow beginning to eat Cheddar sandwiches?

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for the ravine is placed around the letter

parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: A cheese lover wonders whether Cheddar belongs in sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge in Somerset is the famous ravine near the village that gave its name to the cheese; it 'sandwiches' E after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention: any man's name can define a fellow, and this is a common male forename.

clue.text: Drive through American street

parts.note: thru is the informal American spelling of through

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive along a road in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forceful push or propulsion, as in the drive or force of an engine or argument.
